Test Objective: Verify PCIe link training completes successfully in x4 lane configuration
Test Description: Perform PCIe link training for x4 lane width on DM0/DM1 in RC or EP mode. The test initializes the synchronization register to 0x0 then calls link_training_dm0_x4(4) or link_training_dm1_x4(4) based on the compile-time mode configuration.
Pre-conditions:
1. PCIe controller is in reset state
2. PHY is initialized
3. Link partner is present
Test Steps:
1. Write 0x0 to synchronization register at 0xE6004100
2. Call link_training_dm0_x4(4) for DM0_RC/DM0_EP mode OR link_training_dm1_x4(4) for DM1_RC/DM1_EP mode
3. Wait for link training to complete
4. Verify link status via SII register polling
Expected Results:
1. Link training completes without timeout
2. SII register at offset 0xC0 returns status with bits [7:6:4:0] = 0xD1 indicating link up in L0 state
3. Negotiated link width is x4
Pass/Fail Criteria: Link training completes and SII status register reads 0xD1 (link up)

Test Objective: Verify cache coherency control register programming for PCIe
Test Description: Program COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register for both PCIE0 and PCIE1 instances with cache enable settings. Set bits [14:11] and [6:3] to 0xF for write cache and bits [30:27] and [22:19] to 0xF for read cache.
Pre-conditions:
1. Link training completed successfully
2. PCIe controller is accessible
Test Steps:
1. Read mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF
2. Set bits [14:11] to 0xF using set_data()
3. Set bits [6:3] to 0xF using set_data()
4. Write back to COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF
5. Read again and set bits [30:27] to 0xF
6. Set bits [22:19] to 0xF
7. Write back to COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF
8. Repeat steps 1-7 for PCIE1 instance
9. Wait 20 cycles
10. Consolidate all cache bits in single write for PCIE0 and PCIE1
Expected Results:
1. COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register bits [14:11][6:3][30:27][22:19] are all set to 0xF
2. Cache coherency is enabled for both read and write paths
3. Both PCIE0 and PCIE1 instances are configured identically
Register Fields: Write cache enable bits [14:11][6:3], Read cache enable bits [30:27][22:19]
Pass/Fail Criteria: All cache coherency bits are correctly programmed and read back matches expected values

Test Objective: Verify PCIe device Vendor ID is readable through configuration space access
Test Description: Read the Vendor ID from PCIe slave configuration space at offset 0x0 (TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG). The Vendor ID field occupies bits [15:0] and Device ID occupies bits [31:16].
Pre-conditions:
1. Link training completed successfully
2. PCIe link is in L0 state (DLL active)
3. Running in DM0_RC mode
Test Steps:
1. Call read_pcie_slv0_reg(0x0) to read TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG
2. Print the Vendor ID value
3. Verify Vendor ID matches expected value 0x16C3
4. Verify Device ID in upper 16 bits matches expected value 0xABCD
Expected Results:
1. Vendor ID reads as 0x16C3 (bits [15:0])
2. Device ID reads as 0xABCD (bits [31:16])
3. Combined register value is 0xABCD16C3
Pass/Fail Criteria: Vendor ID reads 0x16C3 and Device ID reads 0xABCD

Test Objective: Verify cache coherency disable programming for PCIe

Test Description: Release PHY reset then read 3 PHY registers for both PCIE0 and PCIE1 and verify default values are 0x0.
Pre-conditions:
1. PCIe controller out of reset
2. PHY in reset state
Test Steps:
1. Write 0x01203000 to mizar_PCIE0_SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL to release PHY reset
2. Write 0x01203000 to mizar_PCIE1_SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL
3. For i=0 to 2: read phy0_addr[i] (0xE68860B8 0xE68862B8 0xE68864B8)
4. Apply 16-bit extraction based on address alignment (upper/lower half-word)
5. Compare with phy0_default[i] (0x0)
6. Repeat for phy1_addr[i] (0xE68A60B8 0xE68A62B8 0xE68A64B8)
Expected Results:
1. PHY reset released successfully
2. All 3 PCIE0 PHY registers read default value 0x0
3. All 3 PCIE1 PHY registers read default value 0x0
4. 16-bit extraction logic works correctly
Pass/Fail Criteria: All PHY registers read their expected default reset values after reset release

Test Objective: Verify register write/read with all-ones pattern (0xFFFFFFFF)

Pre-conditions:
1. Reset value check completed
2. All registers accessible
Test Steps:
1. Write 0xFFFFFFFF to all 5 rc0_ctl_addr registers
2. Write 0xFFFFFFFF to all 5 rc1_ctl_addr registers
3. Write (0xFFFFFFFF & sii0_write_mask[i]) to 3 sii0_addr registers
4. Write (0xFFFFFFFF & sii1_write_mask[i]) to 3 sii1_addr registers
5. Release PHY reset
6. Write (0x7BAF & 0x1FFF) to 3 phy0_addr registers
7. Write (0x7BAF & 0x1FFF) to 3 phy1_addr registers
8. Read back all registers and compare
Expected Results:
1. RC registers read back 0xFFFFFFFF
2. SII registers read back (0xFFFFFFFF & write_mask): HEADER2/3=0xFFFFFFFF PHY_CONTROL_23=0xF000F
3. PHY registers read back (0x7BAF & 0x1FFF) = 0x1BAF
4. No data mismatches (err1 = 0)
Registers Accessed: MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, UTILITY_OFF, SII TRANSMIT_HEADER2/3, SII PHY_CONTROL_23, PHY registers
Register Fields: All 32-bit fields for RC/SII; 13-bit masked fields for PHY (mask=0x1FFF)
Register Address/Offset: RC: MSI_CAP offsets; SII: TRANSMIT_HEADER offsets; PHY: 0xE68860B8 etc.
Pass/Fail Criteria: All registers read back written values (with write masks applied)

Test Objective: Verify overall test pass/fail status based on accumulated error counts
Test Description: Check final error counters err1 and err2 to determine overall test result. Test passes only if both counters are zero.
Pre-conditions:
1. All reset value checks completed
2. All write/read pattern checks completed
Test Steps:
1. Evaluate (err2 || err1)
2. Call finish(err2 || err1)
3. If result is 0 test PASSES
4. If result is non-zero test FAILS with accumulated error count
